text:
incident-bot: ALERT: POP ap-northeast1 experiencing elevated packet loss (15-30%) on CDN egress. Impact: some requests 5xx/timeout. Auto-escalation to oncall in 2m.

mike_oncall: saw this. I'm paged. grabbing context.

tara_netops: we're seeing BFD flaps to one upstream provider in ap-northeast1, looks like peering ASN 64520.

mike_oncall: ok start timeline capture. @tara_netops can you paste the upstream traceroutes? also which customer traffic is hitting that POP?

tara_netops: pastebin with outputs: ``traceroute -n 203.0.113.45`` shows hops stalling at 203.0.113.1 then 10%+ loss. BGP neighbor to 203.0.113.2 shows intermittent withdraws.

alex_sre: adding `netstat` and edge logs, seeing retries and increased tail latencies. Routing table shows backup route with higher cost but healthy.

mike_oncall: mitigation idea: divert new connections away from ap-northeast1 POP by updating CDN-edge routing policy to prefer backup POPs in jp-east1 for 10m. Can we apply a quick route policy?

tara_netops: we can push a route preference tweak, but it's noisy. Suggest apply a traffic-split rule at CDN control plane: 70% -> jp-east1, 30% -> ap-northeast1, then 100% if stable.

mike_oncall: do it. @deploy-bot please apply `cdn route-set ap-northeast1 --split 70:30 --reason "mitigate packetloss 1984502468"` and watch.

deploy-bot: Command queued: `cdn route-set ...` - will execute in 15s.

incident-bot: NOTE: customer-impact tag added: "partial request failures, increased latencies for some regions". Severity: P2.

eve_support: heads up to CS: customers in APAC might see timeouts. I'm drafting a short status blurb for live customers.

mike_oncall: good. @eve_support drop the blurb in product-alerts channel and link to status page. Keep ambiguous: "some users" to avoid panic.

tara_netops: route change applied. 69% traffic now offloaded to jp-east1. Observability: packet loss at ap-northeast1 dropped from 22% -> 6% in last 2 minutes.

alex_sre: metrics look better. 5xx rate down 60%. tail p95 latency improved. We'll keep watch for 20m before restoring.

mike_oncall: engaging cloud provider support for the peering ASN. I opened ticket CP-87219. Provider acknowledges flapping and says investigating intermediate metro router.

tara_netops: temporary workaround: we've disabled BFD for that neighbor to reduce withdraws while provider fixes. Will monitor for route churn.

sam_shift_lead: handoff note: if this still active at shift change, escalate to oncall+network lead. Also capture PCAPs from the POP egress for postmortem.

mike_oncall: capturing PCAPs now and uploading to secure bucket: `s3://redwood-incidents/1984502468/pcaps/` - link limited to SRE and netops.

eve_support: posted customer blurb to product-alerts and status.redwood.ai incident page. Short note and ETA 2h while provider investigates.

alex_sre: adding an automatic fallback policy to the CDN config for 30s connection failures -> immediate retry to alternate POP. This reduces observed user impact for streaming workloads.

tara_netops: provider updated: they've isolated a misconfig at a regional router, doing config rollback. They estimate 40m to full remediation.

mike_oncall: action items: 1) Keep split in place for 30m, 2) collect pcap/logs, 3) monitor provider ticket, 4) prepare post-incident notes.

incident-bot: INCIDENT NOTE: Paging suppressed for lower-severity alerts for ap-northeast1 for next 30m due to manual mitigation.

sam_shift_lead: if provider says fixed, we'll gradually shift traffic back over 10m. Call back to coordinate required.

mike_oncall: oncall handoff at 30m: I'll prepare a short Handoff message with what's done and next checks.

mike_oncall: HANDOFF: ap-northeast1 packetloss; mitigation: CDN split (70% jp-east1), BFD disabled for problem neighbor, PCAPs collected, provider ticket CP-87219 open. Monitor p95 latency and 5xx rate. Owner until 1984510068: tara_netops, fallback to sam_shift_lead after that.

incident-bot: Closing note: if any regression, re-open thread or page oncall. :white_check_mark:
